public_rationale: Before the post, Thinking Machines Lab documented deterministic LLM inference and reported 1,000 identical completions after changing its inference kernels. That contradicts the claim that LLMs cannot be deterministic. The same report explains why ordinary inference services can vary even at temperature zero; default variability is compatible with deterministic implementations.
limitations: The evidence is the implementing lab's report, not an independent replication.
The result requires specified inference controls and does not promise identical outputs across arbitrary hardware or software changes.
Deterministic output can still contain factual errors.

statement.excerpt: LLMs will always hallucinate, their outputs are not trustworthy as a result, they cannot be deterministic, and any chance of any mistakes of any kind are unforgivable.
statement.document_title: I Will Never Respect A Website

our_interpretation: The ordinary technical meaning of deterministic is producing identical outputs from identical inputs under fixed model and execution conditions.
The claim denies that deterministic LLM inference is possible; it does not merely describe default behavior of hosted chatbot services.
This is an as-of-publication capability claim without a reporting cycle. The target covers implementations already demonstrated by 2026-04-14, with no lower date supplied by the speaker.
Reproducibility and factual correctness are separate properties.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence that LLM inference necessarily varies despite fixed inputs, model parameters, decoding and execution conditions, with no feasible deterministic implementation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented LLM implementation that provides reproducible inference under specified conditions, supported by implementation details and repeated-output tests.
